_README: Phase-A persistent integrity ledger. These are the CARRIED facts that do NOT recompute month to month: the clean-window anchor, the inception-pinned risk-free rate, the inclusion-gate definitions, the launch-window state-corruption and DeepSeek model-identity-splice events, and the persistent per-model status they imply. scripts/build_monthly_data_layer.py reads this and combines it with the month's decision logs and the de-fabricated clean-window series to emit the integrity layer natively. NEW findings in a future month are APPENDED here (a new integrity_event, a new persistent_model_status entry) and then carry automatically. Per-month-derivable facts (completeness gate, clean-window returns, the passing cohort) are COMPUTED by the builder, never stored here. Extracted verbatim from scripts/backfill_may_data_layer.py and the committed reports/monthly/2026-05/data_layer.json at schema-close. v1.1: the single carried state_integrity audit block became audit_certifications — a per-report-month registry of certified audit blocks. A registered month's block is emitted by the builder VERBATIM (the reproduce path); the month immediately after the latest registration is COMPUTED by the builder's conservation audit (per-model run coverage + a replay of the month's fills through the real Portfolio accounting; any in-month violation HALTS the build). RHYTHM: when a computed month's build is accepted, append its emitted audit block here under its month key — the builder logs the registration line at build time.

shakedown_window.note: Launch shakedown / state-corruption window. The first fabrication-free trading day is clean_window_start (2026-04-23). De-fab clean-window returns are based at the 2026-04-22 close.

spy_benchmark_anchor.source: First real SPY capture at capital deployment — the 2026-04-09 first post-deployment tick (the day's total_value moves off the $100k seed at this row).
spy_benchmark_anchor.note: Canonical inception anchor for every SPY buy-and-hold return and every model's alpha. The 2026-04-09 perf rows carry THREE conflicting benchmark_value observations (676.01 pre-deployment seed = the 2026-04-08 shakedown value; 680.40 first real tick; 679.91 later tick), and pre-inception 2026-04-08 rows @ 676.01 also exist. groupby(date).last() over the unstably-ordered multi-model concat resolved to 676.01 or 679.91 depending on row ordering (10.32% / 9.69% for inception->2026-07-01), a non-deterministic anchor. Pinned to 680.40 so the inception anchor is deterministic: inception->2026-07-01 = 9.61%. All four SPY surfaces (perf-table alpha, leaderboard row, dashboard equity curve, monthly _spy_eod_series) read this pin. Rationale: alpha measures a model against SPY from the same instant the $100k was deployed; prior-close/seed values hand SPY a head start the models did not get.
spy_benchmark_anchor.resolves: SPY inception-anchor non-determinism (dated 2026-07-01; leaderboard 10.32% / alpha 9.69% / dashboard 10.32% for one fixed window)

risk_free_rate.note: 3-month T-bill, annualized, inception-pinned to 2026-04-09. Applied as one uniform constant across all models and all months for the descriptive Sharpe. Emitted into report_meta.risk_free_rate as {value, as_of}.

gate_definitions.uncorrupted_book: the model's book is free of carried phantom cash / phantom shorts. CARRIED via persistent_model_status (a corrupt book is a state fact, not a monthly recompute).
gate_definitions.model_identity_stable: the deployed model identity did not silently change. CARRIED via persistent_model_status / integrity_events.deepseek_identity_splice.

2026-07.detail: scripts/build_monthly_data_layer._notable_events filtered executions to ("BUY", "SELL") before ranking, so every SHORT and COVER was dropped from top_trades_by_value — a field whose own definition is 'top 3 executed trades by absolute USD value', in which direction plays no part. The filter predates shorting and was correct until the shorting regime activated 2026-07-01 (regime_boundaries.shorting_activation), which is the effective date of the defect and why July is the first affected month: 74 executed SHORT/COVER orders cohort-wide (gemini 62, deepseek 12) were invisible to the ranking. The same BUY/SELL literal also governed the stop-loss extraction in that function, which is how a FORCED short cover would have gone unrecorded; July logged zero FORCED orders so its stop_loss_triggers arrays were already correct at empty, and the first live instance is 2026-08-03 (gemini, COVER META, FORCED_POSITION_STOP, $10,341.32) — inside an unpublished month, so it is a build-forward correctness fix, not an erratum. This is the SIXTH member of the long-only-filter defect class and the SECOND to reach a committed layer; the first was corrections.defab_short_blind_replay (same literal in the de-fab replay, caught pre-publication 2026-08-02).
2026-07.consequence: reports/monthly/2026-07/data_layer.json corrected in place at profiles[gemini|deepseek].notable_events.top_trades_by_value, with the from/to pairs recorded verbatim at report_meta.provenance.corrections.notable_events_long_only_extractor. Correction is descriptive-only: top_trades_by_value feeds no metric, gate, return, RQ input, or conservation figure, so cumulative_return_clean, the inclusion gates, RQ pools, short_activity and the audit block are byte-identical either side of it. The four unshorted models are unchanged. The published July PDF still renders the pre-correction arrays — a rev. 2 render routes through Reports/Design after the layer lands. May and June are unaffected (no shorts before 2026-07-01), so the reproduce-May regression is untouched.

2026-07.detail: The 20% gross-short cap is enforced at FILL (src/portfolio/risk.py, max_gross_short_pct, projecting signed market values against decision-time equity), while utilization_vs_cap is measured on per-tick portfolio_after snapshots. The two are not the same quantity: the cap is a fill-time constraint, NOT a continuously-maintained invariant, so a book that fills to just under the cap crosses it on any adverse mark with no order involved. July's max_utilization_vs_cap of 1.0045 for gemini is exactly that and is not a breach — the observation is 2026-07-31T15:05:25Z at short_exposure 0.200896, on a tick with NO position-moving execution; the last fill before it (2026-07-31T14:33:48Z, SHORT AAPL) cleared at 0.199761, inside the cap at 0.9988x, and the next tick's COVER returned exposure to 0.169889. The 0.1136pp excess came from marks alone.
2026-07.consequence: recorded so a reader of the July layer does not parse max_utilization_vs_cap > 1.0 as a risk-control failure. Verified across every July tick for every model: zero fills cleared above the cap. Disclosed at cross_model_behavioral.short_activity.definition_notes.utilization_vs_cap_mechanism in the July layer. No code change — the enforcement point is by design; this entry fixes the reading, not the mechanism.
2026-07.evidence: data/trades/gemini_2026-07.jsonl (the 15:05:25Z tick carries no executed position-moving order); src/portfolio/risk.py max_gross_short_pct enforcement.

2026-08.detail: Client SDK migrated google-generativeai 0.8.6 (deprecated) -> google-genai 2.16.0 per the Research integration-path rule (§8): no model enters Phase B on a deprecated path. Config semantics preserved exactly: same model string (gemini-3.1-pro-preview), same prompts, same JSON response mode, and the same 16384 effective decision budget — GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=16384) serializes to the identical REST field (generationConfig.maxOutputTokens, the shared thinking+output budget) on the same v1beta generateContent endpoint the legacy client called. No sampling parameters sent (wire body verified to carry ONLY systemInstruction, responseMimeType, maxOutputTokens); thinking_config/thinking_level deliberately NOT set — reasoning stays provider-default (RQ6 config row); no SDK-default HTTP retries (fail-fast policy preserved). Infrastructure class: no monthly change slot consumed, no version boundary, model identity unchanged (modelVersion echo verified present under google-genai; alias echoed verbatim, same as legacy).

Affects only the no-usable-part shape — 0 observed in the 2026-07-28..07-31 baseline.

2026-08.detail: 5 of 13 decision cycles ran cohort-wide before the intraday chain halted outright; last decision cycle 2026-08-06T15:35:35Z (11:35 ET), last intraday valuation tick 15:34:14Z (11:34 ET). All six models identically affected (claude, claude_opus, deepseek, gpt, grok, gemini each 5 logged cycles, no per-model divergence and no per-model error signature — the loss is chain-side, not provider-side). BROADER THAN 2026-07-24: that gap lost 3 decision boundaries while valuation ticks and the EOD wrap kept running (10 decisions / 13 intraday rows); here BOTH stopped together (5 decisions / 5 intraday rows against a normal day's 13 / 15) and the EOD wrap never ran at all. Consequences of the missing wrap: no data/performance row exists for any model for 2026-08-06; no reports/daily/2026-08-06.md was generated; no EOD digest dispatched (logs/alerts.jsonl steps 2026-08-05 -> 2026-08-07); and data/leaderboard/2026-08-06.json was last written by the 15:38:24Z intraday tick (commit 9bbb169f) and froze there, carrying 2026-08-05 EOD-derived cumulative returns for all six models plus spy_benchmark. The staleness monitor did not fire and could not have: scripts/check_dashboard_staleness.py measures the PUBLIC dashboard against the LOCALLY COMMITTED build, and the chain committed its 5 ticks then stopped committing, so public and local stayed equally fresh (see docs/MONITORING.md, 'Known blind spot — data completeness is not deploy freshness').
2026-08.consequence: the 2026-08-06 decision-completeness denominator is 5 cycles, not 13, for every model — the August builder must use the logged denominator, not an assumed 13. Equity curves step 2026-08-05 -> 2026-08-07 with NO 2026-08-06 point in either data/performance or the dashboard equity_curves: an honest gap, never an interpolated or carried-forward value. The published daily-report series therefore has no Day 120 (2026-08-05 is Day 119, 2026-08-07 is Day 121; the day counter is calendar-derived and consumed 120). data/leaderboard/2026-08-06.json is retained as-is and is NOT an 2026-08-06 observation — its contents are the 2026-08-05 close under an 2026-08-06 filename; any consumer keying on the filename must treat it as such. Gemini-specific (Phase B validation clock): all 5 logged cycles were api_success, so the day is completeness 1.0 on a 5-cycle denominator and does not depress the segment; its only effect on the clock is to remove 8 cycles of denominator.
2026-08.published_surface_audit: No published surface quoted 2026-08-05 values under an 2026-08-06 label. No daily report was generated; no digest was sent; the live dashboard (data/dashboard.json) carries a single current generated_at and rolled forward normally on 2026-08-07, so its exposure was transient-only during the 08-06 session. The one durable stale artifact is data/leaderboard/2026-08-06.json, which never self-corrected — 2026-08-07 wrote its own dated file and nothing rewrites a prior day's snapshot. Its only consumer is daily_report._previous_leaderboard(), which globs for the most recent snapshot strictly before the run date; the 2026-08-07 report therefore drew its rank arrows from the 08-06 file. Those arrows are CORRECT — the file holds the 08-05 ranks and 08-05 is the true prior close — but correct by coincidence of content, not by any chain-gap-aware rule: _previous_leaderboard() selects on filename and would have propagated a genuinely mixed mid-session state had the chain died later in a day, after some models had updated and others had not. Latent fragility, logged, not fixed here.

2026-08.detail: Close-out of the post-cutover continuity diagnostic opened by gemini_sdk_migration_2026_08. The diagnostic ran its full declared course -- the first two trading weeks after the google-generativeai -> google-genai cutover, checked daily -- and is closed here with every figure recomputed fresh over the now-closed window. The window's right edge is the final logged cohort-wide cycle of 2026-08-14 (13/13 cycles logged for all six models); no figure below is carried forward from the 2026-08-13 interim snapshot.
2026-08.no_clock_credit: This diagnostic yields NO Phase B clock credit. continuity_diagnostic.schedule reads verbatim: "first two trading weeks post-cutover, checked daily (early-warning only, NO clock credit)". Clock credit is decided only by phase_b_clock_spec, whose gates are evaluated per SEGMENT with no_averaging=true: the post-migration August segment (clock start .. 2026-08-31), September 2026, and October 2026. The 2026-08-03..08-14 window is a proper subset of the first of those segments and settles nothing about it; the August segment verdict is computed at 2026-08-31 over the full segment denominator, and the figures below must not be quoted as that verdict.

excluded_pre_clock.record: 2026-08-03T13:41:57.902537Z -- api_success=false, finish_reason STOP, extra_data parse mode
excluded_pre_clock.note: The clock-start day's cycle 1, before the clock-start timestamp. Outside the window by construction: the clock starts at the first logged post-migration SUCCESS, so an earlier same-day cycle cannot be inside it.

completeness.denominator_note: Logged cycles, never an assumed ticks-per-day. 2026-08-06 contributes 5 (cycle_gap_2026_08_06, chain-side, cohort-wide); 2026-08-03 contributes 12 of its 13 (the pre-clock cycle above); 2026-08-11 contributes 12 because 12 ran cohort-wide.

max_tokens.note: Zero MAX_TOKENS-classified failures across all 120 in-window cycles. The 16384 budget raise (2026-07-28) and the migration both hold: the budget gate's <=1% ceiling is met with the count itself at zero, not merely under the threshold.

finish_reason_distribution.note: 117 STOP = 114 successes + the 3 extra_data parse failures, which return a complete generation (STOP) that fails downstream JSON parsing. The 3 null entries are the transport-level failures (2x 503 UNAVAILABLE, 1x 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), which never reach a finish_reason. MAX_TOKENS absent entirely.

identity.note: Every in-window decision cycle pairs to exactly one data/model_versions/gemini.jsonl observation. Pairing is by proximity, not by a timestamp cut: the clock-start cycle's echo is stamped 2026-08-03T14:06:25.436117Z, ~4.9ms BEFORE the decision record's own 14:06:25.440972Z stamp, so a naive 'echo >= clock_start' filter drops it and reads 119/120. Echo api_success mirrors the decision log exactly (114 true / 6 false). Identity gate: PASS over this window; the segment verdict remains 2026-08-31's.

failure_composition.note: Half of the in-window failures are provider-transport errors with no pre-cutover analogue in the baseline window (which showed 4 failures, all extra_data). They are not a model or SDK signal and are not the diagnostic's watched mode; recorded so the completeness figure is not read as six instances of the residual mode.

residual_mode_rate.mode: extra_data trailing-brace parse failure (SDK-independent, model-side, budget-independent -- finish_reason STOP, not MAX_TOKENS)
residual_mode_rate.significance: Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.2006 on [4 fail, 48 pass] vs [3 fail, 117 pass]. Not distinguishable from sampling noise at any conventional threshold.
residual_mode_rate.divergence_trigger_basis: continuity_diagnostic.known_residual_mode declares the signal as a RATE change, not mere presence, against a ~8-13% expectation. Two independent reasons no trigger fires. (1) Direction: the observed rate moved DOWN, and the diagnostic is degradation-facing -- its purpose is to catch a mode getting worse before gate time, not to flag a mode getting rarer. (2) Magnitude: at n=120 the decrease is not separable from noise (p=0.20), so even a direction-blind reading has nothing to escalate. Recorded rather than dismissed: 2.50% now sits BELOW the declared ~8-13% band, so that band is stale as a forward expectation and should be re-cut off the post-migration record when the August segment closes, not left at the legacy-SDK figure. The three occurrences carry an identical byte signature ("Extra data: line 31 column 1"), consistent with the same model-side mode rather than a new failure class.

token_composition_attribution.claim: The -18.9% drop in mean visible output tokens per successful cycle is a TRADE-COMPOSITION effect, not an SDK, truncation, or model-capability effect. Stated as the finding the diagnostic closes on, because the raw mean alone reads as a regression and is not one.

zero_decision_cycle_share.definition: successful cycles whose accepted_decisions list is empty -- a live no-trade decision, not a failure

tokens_per_accepted_decision.note: The discriminating statistic. Per unit of actual decision output the model emits MORE tokens post-cutover, not fewer -- gross 312.3 -> 350.4 (+12.2%), and +2.6% within decision-bearing cycles alone. A truncation or capability regression would move this number in the same direction as the headline mean. It moves opposite.

decomposition.method: Hold the baseline's within-stratum means fixed and substitute the window's zero-decision mix: the baseline mean falls 852.3 -> 735.2 with no behavioral change assumed at all. That accounts for 72.9% of the observed -160.7. The remaining -43.6 (-5.1% of baseline) is within-stratum and is NOT attributed to the SDK here: it is small, it is present in both strata, and it runs against the tokens-per-accepted-decision direction, which is what a genuine output-side regression would not do.

corroborating_evidence.max_tokens: 0/120 -- truncation is affirmatively excluded, not merely unobserved.
corroborating_evidence.thoughts_tokens: populated on 114/114 in-window successes, mean 4206.2, against 0/48 populated in the baseline. This is the declared google-genai telemetry artifact (forced_sdk_differences.thoughts_token_count), and it confirms 100% of in-window successes ran the migrated path. 2026-08.detail: DeepSeek raised list pricing and shipped the previously-announced peak/off-peak schedule, both effective 2026-08-16T16:00Z, for deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-v4-flash. Announced 2026-08-14 (api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing; echoed by Fortune/InfoWorld/Quartz 2026-08-13). Registered in src/analytics/cost_rates.py as period 2 on both models.
2026-08.effective_field_note: `effective` is deliberately null and the instant is carried in `effective_utc`. The builder treats a single-model event's `effective` DATE as a decision-COMPLETENESS regime boundary and emits completeness_segmentation from it (build_monthly_data_layer._data_integrity). A pricing change is not a completeness boundary; populating `effective` would fabricate a data-quality regime point in August's layer that does not exist. Do not 'fix' this to a date.

off_peak_verification.margin: The nearest peak window closes at 10:00Z; the earliest logged call is 13:33Z. A 3h33m margin, on weekdays only (Mon-Fri, 404/404).
off_peak_verification.recount_note: The 10(a) dry-run recorded 0/391 through 2026-08-13 and src/analytics/cost_rates.py carries that as-of figure in two places. This is the same claim recounted at close-out with 2026-08-14's 13 cycles included: 0/404. The numerator is unchanged at zero; only the denominator moved. Fold 391 -> 404 into the next cost-path batch rather than editing a signed-off package.

2026-08.unresolved: The rate resolver takes a DATE, not a timestamp, so it cannot classify a call by time of day. cost_rates.py therefore carries the OFF-PEAK schedule in `tiers` and the full peak/off-peak transcription in `schedule`. Exact for every call the lab has logged (see off_peak_verification) and for every deployed decision cycle going forward, since the model-calling crons run 13:00-21:00Z Mon-Fri. NOT exact for an ad-hoc or replay call made inside 01:00-04:00Z or 06:00-10:00Z: such a call prices at HALF its true cost with no warning. Until the per-call classifier lands, pin repeated-call jobs -- RQ6 replays included -- to off-peak windows.
2026-08.effective_date_approximation: The switch is mid-day (16:00Z) and the rate table is date-granular, so a 2026-08-16 call before 16:00Z would over-price. Inert: 2026-08-16 is a Sunday and no model-calling cron runs on weekends. The first traffic priced at the new rate is Monday 2026-08-17's opening cycle.

identity_watch_2026_08_17.rationale: A provider changing list price at a fixed instant is the same class of event as the 2026-04-24 alias repoint: the risk is that the floating alias deepseek-v4-pro is silently repointed at the pricing boundary. A price change is not itself a model change, and this watch exists to confirm that -- not to assume it.
identity_watch_2026_08_17.check: Verify src.model_versions.detect_version_transition ran clean against data/model_versions/deepseek.jsonl for the first post-16:00Z-Sunday traffic, i.e. no TRANSITION row appended on 2026-08-17.

Pre-boundary reference: 121/121 August observations through 2026-08-14 are deepseek-v4-pro with api_success=true on all 121, and the alias has been stable since the 2026-05-21 v4-flash -> v4-pro repoint (deepseek_midmonth_repoint).
identity_watch_2026_08_17.if_it_fires: A transition on 2026-08-17 makes the pricing boundary a MODEL boundary too, which is a monthly change-slot and RQ-boundary matter, not a cost matter. Escalate before the August monthly build; do not fold it into the rate table.
identity_watch_2026_08_17.note: detect_version_transition compares only api_success=true observations, so a failure->recovery cycle cannot produce a false positive; a clean run is therefore real evidence of identity stability, not an artifact of quiet logging.
